Wilderness of Jeruel
jeh-ROO-el
proper noun
Hebrew midbar Yeruel, the desert of Jeruel (perhaps “founded of God” or “fear of God”), a waste tract in the wilderness of Judah between Tekoa and the cliff of Ziz above En-gedi.

📖 Biblical Definition

When a great multitude of Moab and Ammon and mount Seir came against Jehoshaphat, the king feared, and set himself to seek the LORD, and proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah. As the people stood before the LORD with their little ones, the Spirit came upon Jahaziel, who cried: “Ye shall not need to fight in this battle: set yourselves, stand ye still, and see the salvation of the LORD… for the battle is not yours, but God’s.” On the morrow they went forth toward the wilderness of Jeruel (2Ch 20:16), and there they found their enemies already fallen one upon another, so that none escaped. And Judah’s part was to sing: they appointed singers unto the LORD, that should praise the beauty of holiness, saying, Praise the LORD, for his mercy endureth for ever; and when they began to sing and to praise, the LORD set ambushments against the foe. The wilderness of Jeruel is the field where faith learns that its warfare is the LORD’s, and that praise goes up before the victory is seen. Here is the gospel pattern: the outnumbered people, unable to save themselves, stand still and behold the salvation of God, and give Him the songs of the delivered. So the believer, hemmed in by enemies too strong for him, sets himself to seek the LORD, stands still, and sings, for the battle is not his but God’s.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A desert tract in Judah above En-gedi where the LORD Himself routed the Moab-Ammon coalition against Jehoshaphat while Judah’s singers praised (2Ch 20:16); a witness that the battle is the LORD’s and that faith praises before the victory.

WILDERNESS OF JERUEL, a desert tract in Judah above En-gedi.

There Jehoshaphat met the great host of Moab, Ammon, and Seir (2Ch 20:16).

Jahaziel prophesied, The battle is not yours, but God’s.

Judah’s appointed singers praised, and the LORD set ambushments against the foe.

A witness that faith stands still, sings, and sees the salvation of the LORD.

📖 Key Scripture

Psa 46:1 — "To the chief Musician for the sons of Korah, A Song upon Alamoth. God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble."

Psa 46:4 — "There is a river, the streams whereof shall make glad the city of God, the holy place of the tabernacles of the most High."

Isa 43:2 — "When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee."

Isa 40:31 — "But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

No modern redefinition attends this desert; the truth to recover is that the LORD fights for those who seek Him, and faith praises before the deliverance appears.

expand to see more

The wilderness of Jeruel is a real place in the Judean desert, and the history of Jehoshaphat’s deliverance stands unshaken in the record.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the salvation of God’s people is God’s own work, not theirs. Jehoshaphat did not muster a cleverer army; he set himself to seek the LORD, proclaimed a fast, and set the singers before the host. Faith’s posture is to stand still and behold; faith’s music begins before the enemy falls. Recover this against every gospel of self-salvation: the battle is not ours, but God’s.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Jeruel likely means “founded of God” or “fear of God”; the desert so named became the theatre of God’s own victory.

expand to see more

Jeruel — Hebrew Yeruel, perhaps “founded of God” or “fear of God.”

Midbar, wilderness, an untilled tract fit for pasture or waste.

A desert region of Judah toward the cliff of Ziz and En-gedi.

Near the ascent by which the invading host came up against Jehoshaphat.

Distinct from the valley of Berachah, where Judah blessed the LORD after the victory.

Usage

"Judah went forth toward the wilderness of Jeruel to meet the foe."

"In the wilderness of Jeruel the singers praised before the battle was won."

"The battle is not yours, but God’s — the lesson of Jeruel."
